circles.name: The Peninsula
circles.note: The kingdoms of the north and the ṭāʾifas of the frontier: the marches of Book V. From September 1420 Qashtāla is four towns on the Cantabrian coast, beside the petty kings of Jillīqiya, Ashturiyās and Nabarra in the mountains.

circles.name: The Maghrib
circles.note: The Muslim West across the water: the Marīnids twice beaten, Tlemcen their fief, the Ḥafṣids of Tunis.

circles.name: The Mashriq
circles.note: The Muslim East, where three empires have risen: the Mamlūk sultan at Cairo, al-Andalus's one ally there; the house of ʿUthmān at Constantinople, kin to the Emperor's wife; and Tīmūr at Samarqand, who holds everything from Tabrīz to Kāshghar.

circles.name: The Lands of the Franks
circles.note: Latin Christendom beyond the Pyrenees and across the sea. From 1 December 1428 England and France have one king, the English Edward, and English Toulouse holds Languedoc to the Pyrenees; beyond them the Emperor, the Pope and the cities of Italy.

circles.name: The Land of the Blacks
circles.note: Beyond the Sahara, where the gold comes from: the mansā of Mālī.

farCapitals._note: Capitals beyond the wide chart's frame, in its coordinates (game pixels from its top-left corner), measured from the game's locations.png.
